claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
A preformed coherent Ti-rich/mixed-metal oxide scale retards oxygen ingress in oxidizing environments.
A preformed Ti-rich/mixed-metal oxide scale retards degradation in reducing environments.
Disruption or spallation of the oxide scale accelerates underlying oxidation in oxidizing environments.
Disruption of the oxide scale promotes internal oxidation under reducing conditions.
Accelerated oxidation or internal oxidation produces localized damage accumulation.
Localized damage accumulation can ultimately cause catastrophic failure.
The as-built alloy has a moderately rough surface.
The untreated as-built surface is prone to non-uniform oxide formation during high-temperature exposure.
Controlled pre-oxidation or passivation can form a uniform, adherent Ti-rich/mixed-metal oxide scale.
Differential thermal expansion can destabilize the oxide scale and cause spallation.
Incomplete oxide coverage can destabilize the scale and cause spallation.
Scale spallation exposes the substrate to rapid oxidation along critical microstructural features.
Under reducing conditions, the absence of a stable oxide layer permits internal oxidation.
Under reducing conditions, the absence of a stable oxide layer permits void nucleation at the metal-gas interface.
Internal oxidation or interfacial void nucleation produces stress concentrations.
Stress concentrations caused by internal oxidation or voids lead to premature failure.
Passivated samples will exhibit delayed crack initiation relative to untreated samples.
Passivated samples will degrade more slowly than untreated samples.
The proposed governing mechanism applies from 700 to 900 °C in both moderately oxidizing and reducing gas atmospheres.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis assigns a protective role to the preformed oxide in reducing environments, whereas the reducing-environment mechanism invokes the absence of an inherently stable oxide layer. It does not clarify whether this absence applies only to untreated samples or whether the preformed scale is expected to become unstable.
